messages:
maya: Heads up — bringing up a new HF model (hf-org/new-chat-lite) and the Redwood conversion flagged missing specials. The fast tokenizer shipped a tokenizer.json but no tokenizer_config.json, and our onboarding script assumes tokenizer_config for special tokens.

sam: ugh, we've seen that before. fast tokenizer usually encodes specials in tokenizer.json (added_tokens / special_tokens_map). slow/py tokenizers use tokenizer_config.json keys like 'special_tokens_map'. Which fields are mismatching here?

maya: Example from the model artifacts:
```
# tokenizer.json (fast) snippet
"added_tokens": [ {"id": 50256, "special": true, "content": "<|system|>"} ],
"special_tokens_map": {"pad_token": "<|pad|>", "bos_token": "<|bos|>"}

# tokenizer_config.json (missing) -> file not present
```
So conversion fell back to default specials and the chat template->role mapping got misaligned. Conversation flows showed system messages being treated as user.

arjun: our converter currently does: prefer tokenizer_config.json.special_tokens_map else fallback to tokenizer.json.special_tokens_map. But the bug is it only looks for top-level keys in tokenizer.json and the HF fast tokenizer nests them under 'model' or inside different shapes. Need more robust detection.

lin: I can repro locally. Sometimes tokenizer.json uses keys like `model.special_tokens_map` or `tokenizer['added_tokens']` with different shapes. We should: 1) detect fast vs slow by presence of "tokenizer.json"; 2) if fast, parse for both added_tokens and special_tokens_map variants; 3) unify into canonical map for Redwood.

maya: Agreed. Also we should validate chat_template placeholders against the canonical specials. Right now if pad/bos/sep mismatch, the chat parsing test passes but semantic evals fail.

sam: Proposed patch: converter changes
```
- if exists(tokenizer_config.json): use special_tokens_map
- else: load tokenizer.json and run extract_fast_tokenizer_specials(tokenizer_json)
+ extract_fast_tokenizer_specials should look for: 
+  - top-level "special_tokens_map"
+  - top-level "added_tokens" entries with "special": true
+  - nested under "model" or "data" keys (best-effort)
+ Emit a warning with model name when we had to heuristically reconstruct specials.
```
This will avoid silent wrong defaults.

arjun: also add a unit test fixture: minimal tokenizer.json with nested model->specials and assert converter yields same canonical map as tokenizer_config.json fixture. I'll add a few edge cases (missing pad_token, duplicates, and conflicting ids).

lin: CI note: the onboarding pipeline currently fails silently for these models — we should make the job fail on heuristics (i.e., if we had to reconstruct specials, mark check as WARN, and for new models treat WARN as FAIL until verified). That will force manual review for edge cases.

ci-bot: onboarding/hf-convert job #487 failed: canonical_specials_check WARN for hf-org/new-chat-lite. See: https://ci.redwood.com/jobs/487

maya: @sam @arjun @lin can we get a patch today? This one caused a small eval regression on chat benchmarks (system messages dropped).

sam: on it. I'll open a draft PR and include the warning/heuristic metrics endpoint so we can see how many models hit heuristics over the last 6 months.

arjun: I'll add the unit tests and a small dataset eval to catch role-shift regressions.

lin: I'll update CI to fail new-model onboarding on WARN and add a backlog task to re-audit previously onboarded models (we should surface candidates where tokenizer_config.json was missing).

maya: Thanks — please drop PR links here when ready. Also add a short blurb to the migration guide for model owners: "If your model uses a fast tokenizer, include tokenizer_config.json with special_tokens_map or ensure tokenizer.json explicitly lists special tokens (added_tokens)." :memo:

sam: draft PR -> https://git.redwood/eng/hf-converter/pulls/102 (wip). Tests incoming. :sparkles:

arjun: added unit tests branch -> https://git.redwood/eng/hf-converter/branches/feature/robust-specials-detection

lin: CI rule change MR -> https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/781

maya: great. I'll re-run the failing evals once the PR lands.

ci-bot: job #488 triggered by sam: run tests + new-model-checks.

sam: pinging @platform for telemetry: can we get a histogram of how many models lacked tokenizer_config.json in prod? that will help prioritize re-audits.

maya: looping in @sam to confirm telemetry ask -> thanks. We'll follow up once we have numbers. :pray:
